subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Tea Bag vs. Loose Leaf
description: A quick win: understand Tea Bag vs. Loose Leaf.

hook.text: 96% of all tea drunk in Britain uses tea bags. Loose leaf is a tiny niche despite being vastly better quality.

buildup.text: Tea bags were invented accidentally in 1908 when American merchant Thomas Sullivan sent samples in silk pouches.

discovery.text: Bags use 'fannings' and 'dust'—tiny broken leaf particles that brew fast but lack the complexity of whole leaves.

twist.text: Convenience won over quality. Tea bags turned a slow, skilled ritual into a 2-minute microwave-ready commodity.

climax.text: A growing 'loose leaf revival' movement argues that proper tea is worth the extra 3 minutes of effort.

punchline.text: Fast and convenient beat slow and delicious—for now. Loose leaf fights back.

quiz.question: What type of tea leaf is typically used in tea bags?
options: Fannings and dust—tiny broken leaf particles
